title: I Give You Thanks with All My Heart

verses.text: I give You thanks with all my heart; before the gods I sing Your praises.
I bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness; You have exalted Your name and Your word above all else.
On the day I called, You answered me; You emboldened me and strengthened my soul.
All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O LORD, when they hear the words of Your mouth.
They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great.
Though the LORD is on high, He attends to the lowly; but the proud He knows from afar.
If I walk in the midst of trouble, You preserve me from the anger of my foes; You extend Your hand, and Your right hand saves me.
The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever— do not abandon the works of Your hands.

context.author: The title names David. Psalms 138-145 are the last group of David’s psalms in the book.
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: “I give You thanks with all my heart; before the gods I sing Your praises. I bow down toward Your holy temple and give thanks to Your name for Your loving devotion and Your faithfulness” (vv.1-2). “On the day I called, You answered me; You emboldened me and strengthened my soul” (v.3). David looks ahead to the nations: “All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O LORD, when they hear the words of Your mouth” (v.4). “Though the LORD is on high, He attends to the lowly” (v.6). “If I walk in the midst of trouble, You preserve me” (v.7). “The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me. O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever— do not abandon the works of Your hands” (v.8).
context.custom: Praising God “before the gods” means praising Him openly in a world full of other gods and the kings who served them. Israelites far from Jerusalem prayed facing toward the Temple (1 Kings 8:29-30; Daniel 6:10).
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 139: O LORD, You have searched me and known me.
context.timelineBible: Paul wrote, “He who began a good work in you will carry it on to completion until the day of Christ Jesus” (Philippians 1:6), like v.8. James writes, “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble” (James 4:6), like v.6.

translation.meaning: To complete, bring to an end.

gospelParallels.note: He will carry it on to completion.
The kings of the earth bring their glory.

otBackground.note: The High One dwells with the lowly.

overview.summary: David thanks God wholeheartedly before every rival power, for He answered and strengthened him; the kings of the earth will praise Him, and He will complete His purpose for His servant.

archaeology.t: Kings like Mesha of Moab praised their own gods for victory.
Synagogues were later built facing Jerusalem.

overview.discussion: “The LORD will fulfill His purpose for me” (v.8). What unfinished work in my life am I trusting God to complete?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (all 150 in the app). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: David
overview.audience: God, before the gods and kings
